title: 1942 FBI file: Laurel Canyon address, Norfolk, compromat
place_text: Laurel Canyon, Los Angeles; Norfolk, Virginia

tellings.quote: A clue might be found in a 1942 FBI file on Brown. The file shows Brown living in Laurel Canyon on Wonderland Boulevard.

plain: An FBI file on the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, kept in 1942 and 1943, places him "in Laurel Canyon on Wonderland Boulevard" in Los Angeles, according to Michels, who offers it as "a clue" that also points toward Norfolk, Virginia and toward compromising material that could be used against someone. Michels tells this himself in his film about Brown, a scientist he says built flying-saucer-like devices for the government, drawing on the writers Paul Schatzkin and Paul LaViolette. What the clue is meant to show is about the hidden side of Brown's life and work.
